THE SPEC'S KILL CONDITION (verbatim, what_kills_it):
 "a cusp or K <= 0 (no one-over-distance pull at the atom's size at stand-ins: the hydrogen path is then first-order only and the card should
  be re-weighed); or a +-0.25 coefficient below 0.75 of the averaging value at 2 sigma"

MODEL (premises, read as data): H = -J6 sum_hex (F_h + F_h^dagger) on the two-on (ice) patterns of a supplied periodic diamond block; F_h flips an
alternating six-ring (keeps every site at two on). J6 = 1 is the unit. No diagonal term (V = 0): "pure" per the spec; the native flippable-ring price
(about 4e-4 J6, INSIGHT_AC_2) and the carrier term on all-on six-rings (0.21 J6 per all-on ring, I1 check) are left out and named. One sign (I1, PROVED
on file): sign-free. Sector: M = sum_links sigma_l b_l (sigma = +1 for ON = arrow A->B, b_l the bond vector in units a/4); uniform-flux sector mu means
M = (4 N_A mu, 0, 0) exactly (every link carries mean arrow mu; FA's definition, its uniform crystal has M = 4 N_A). Ring flips never change M.

MY READINGS (registered now, before any numbers):
 RA1 K := [E0(1/4) - E0(0)] / (N x (1/4)^2) per site (primary); K(1/8) likewise from the 1/8 sector (secondary). E0(mu) = the projected ground
     energy (mixed estimator) of the ring-flip component holding the sector's start pattern. Errors: block-averaged statistical errors of each run;
     independent runs combined in quadrature.
 RA2 "Quadratic or cusp": R := [E0(1/4)-E0(0)] / [E0(1/8)-E0(0)]. Quadratic gives 4 (3.95 with FA's quartic term), a pure cusp gives 2.
     QUADRATIC if R - 2 sigma_R > 3; CUSP if R + 2 sigma_R < 3; else UNDETERMINED. Also reported: a = 16 dE(1/8)/N - 4 dE(1/4)/N (the |mu| coefficient
     of a fit a|mu| + b mu^2), and b.
 RA3 Kill (a) MET if, on the largest block that passes every gate, K (central) <= 0 or the verdict is CUSP. NOT MET if K - 2 sigma_K > 0 AND QUADRATIC.
     Otherwise NOT DETERMINED (reported as that, never as a pass).
 RA4 Size of K: K / 0.49 (the registered reference K1 = 2 Gamma J6, Gamma = 0.245) AND K / K1_block, with K1_block = [E_EW(1/4) - E_EW(0)] / (N/16)
     measured on the same block, same sectors, by my own equal-weight sampler (E_EW = -<N_alt> in equal weights).
 RB1 Part (b) observable as in FG and its check: classes of the walker-partner minimum-image separation, 8 bins of 2 bonds from 4 bonds
     ([4,6), [6,8), ..., [16,18), [18,19.5]); y(c) = [ln H+(c)/H-(c) - ln H+(c1)/H-(c1)] / (2 mu), mu = 0.25. Theory: 8 Gamma [G(c) - G(c1)]
     - 12 Gamma [|r|^2(c) - |r|^2(c1)] / N_links, class averages weighted by the pooled (+ and -) histogram; G = the zero-mean pseudo-inverse of the
     block's graph Laplacian (own CG). s := weighted least-squares slope THROUGH THE REFERENCE of y(c) + 12 Gamma d|r|^2(c)/N_links on dG(c), Gamma = 0.245,
     weights = 1/(jackknife variance of each class). sigma_s by delete-one-batch jackknife over the union of + and - batches (class correlations
     included). Also reported: GLS with the jackknife covariance; unweighted free-offset R^2 over the 8 classes; chain-pair scatter.
 RB2 Kill (b) MET if s + 2 sigma_s < 0.75 x 1.96 = 1.47 (8 Gamma's own +-0.08 stated beside it). Against the +-0.5 value: d = s - 1.66,
     sigma_d = sqrt(sigma_s^2 + 0.19^2); "tilt-stable within 25 percent" = |d| <= 0.415. Extrapolation s(0) = [4 s(0.25) - 1.66] / 3, error propagated.
 RB3 "Inside the liquid": f(+-0.25) within 0.01 of f0 +- 0.058 x 0.25 and the ring-flip acceptance above half its value at the other sign; an ensemble
     that orders is VOID (kept, not used).

PLAN (a) - SIGN-FREE PROJECTION (own code, python3 -I, pure Python):
 Blocks (supplied inputs, all inside 432-1,728 sites, each holding mu = 1/8 and 1/4 exactly along x): C4 = conventional 4^3 cubes (512 sites; winding
 quantum dmu = 1/32), P8 = primitive 8^3 cells (1,024 sites; 1/32), C6 = conventional 6^3 cubes (1,728 sites; 1/72). DEVIATION: the 432-site primitive 6^3
 block is not used: its winding quantum along a cubic axis is 1/18, so neither mu = 1/8 nor 1/4 exists on it exactly.
 Sector patterns: zero-flux layered crystal, melted by non-winding directed loops, then exactly 4/4/9 (mu = 1/8) or 8/8/18 (mu = 1/4) x-winding loops
 each raising M_x by one quantum, re-melted by non-winding loops; then ring flips only (the Hamiltonian's own moves).
 Method: continuous-time Green's-function projection by uniformisation (Poisson number of ring flips per interval, weight N_alt/Lambda per flip),
 guiding function = equal weights (local energy -N_alt), fixed population P with comb reconfiguration each interval, mixed estimator with the
 Calandra-Sorella correction (products of Lp average weights); walkers start from equal-weight samples, so E_mix(0) = E_EW and E_mix(tau) must fall
 monotonically to E0.
 Validation FIRST: all two-on patterns of small periodic hosts (16-24 sites) enumerated; ring-flip components with <= 256 states diagonalised exactly
 (Lanczos with full reorthogonalisation, cross-checked by power iteration); the projection compared on E0 and on the exact curve E_mix(tau).
 Pilot at mu = 0 ONLY (timing, projection time, population behaviour) before an addendum fixes P, interval, tau_eq and lengths. No sector difference is
 computed before that addendum is locked.

GATES (applied at every size; a failed gate voids that size's K; no override):
 G1 integrity: at every check (>= 10 per run) every walker has every site at exactly two on, M equal to the sector's exact value, and ring codes equal to
    a fresh recount from the links.
 G2 validation: on every validation component |E0_proj - E0_ED| <= 3 sigma + 1e-3 |E0_ED|, and E_mix(tau) within 3 sigma of the exact curve at
    tau = 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 at >= 90 percent of the points. If G2 fails anywhere: no production run.
 G3 variational: E0(mu) below E_EW(mu) by more than 3 sigma in every sector.
 G4 convergence: mixed-estimator means over the second and last thirds of the measurement window agree within 2.5 sigma (combined).
 G5 population: Calandra-Sorella corrected and uncorrected sector differences agree within 2 sigma; on C4 also population P against P/2 within 2 sigma
    for both differences.
 G6 health: mean per-interval effective population (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 >= 0.5 P; no walker frozen (N_alt = 0).
STOP RULES: part (a) production stops at 30 CPU-minutes (sizes not reached reported as not run). Part (b) gets what remains of 90 CPU-minutes minus a
5-minute reserve; planned >= 1e8 steps per sign (4 x FG's 2.5e7); if its pilot shows 1e8 per sign does not fit, I run what fits and say so.
Seeds: validation 5601-5609; pilot 5611-5619; part (a) production 5621-5649; equal-weight sampler 5651-5659; part (b) pilot 5661, + chains 5671-5679,
- chains 5681-5689.

PLAN (b) - SECOND TILT (own code): L = 24 primitive block (27,648 sites; FA/FG geometry); pinned partner = A site at one on-link; walker = B site at
one on-link moving by two-flip moves (through-partner moves null); window 4-19.5 bonds; bias (R_old/R_new)^2; environment = tilted single ring flips
(global plus a fixed ball round the partner), symmetric proposals, Metropolis with exp(+-mu dN_alt); melt by non-winding loops at mu = 0 before the pair
is placed; several independent chains per sign; batches for the jackknife.

RECALLED, UNVERIFIED (classified, not results): pure six-ring exchange (V = 0) on the diamond block lies inside the U(1) Coulomb phase of quantum ice (liquid
for about -0.5 < V/J < 1, RK point at V = J where every sector is degenerate); there the uniform-flux energy is quadratic, in an ordered phase linear (a cusp);
the pair energy is -4 K G(R) (Gaussian theory). My own reasoning (PROPOSED): Hellmann-Feynman from the RK point gives K = int_0^1 2 Gamma(V) dV with
2 Gamma(1) = K1, which suggests K >= K1 if the ground state's flux sensitivity grows as V falls.

plain_summary: One model family, unchecked, on ready-made blocks at placeholder values. The question: does the pull between opposite charges survive in the network's true lowest-energy state, at the atom's own size? A bounded run, first checked against exact answers on small cases, measured the energy cost of a steady flow through the block. The cost is positive and grows with the square of the flow, as a one-over-distance pull needs, with no sign of a sharp kink. It is about nine-tenths of the first-order estimate, so the pull at atom size is slightly weaker than assumed, but present. Every quality check passed only on the smallest block; on larger blocks some failed, so a checker should repeat it there. A second test of the old measuring trick, at half the tilt, gave the full estimated strength, so the earlier shortfall looks like tilt bias or noise.
